# Independent comparator review — 17 October 2026

Scope: read-only review of the original Fieldguide version 0.18.0 questionnaire and scoring against primary public documentation. No student data was submitted to outside services. No commercial assessment items were copied. This is a methodological comparison, not a psychometric validation study or endorsement.

## What “consistent with established practice” can mean

Fieldguide has 60 original activity-interest questions, evenly split across six RIASEC themes (10 each), plus 12 experience/confidence cards, values and work-context reflections, and eight follow-up questions per chosen field. Its architecture separates interest from confidence and financial feasibility, preserves alternative paths, and gives explanations. Those are defensible exploration design choices. Similar question counts and theme names do not establish equivalence to a validated inventory.

[O*NET’s current Interest Profiler overview](https://www.onetcenter.org/IP.html) distinguishes the 30-item Mini-IP from the 60-item Short Form, describes six RIASEC interests, and makes clear that these tools concern appealing work activities. It also provides a Career Starter worksheet for people starting education/training. My Next Move’s current assessment URL redirects to [onetinterestprofiler.org](https://onetinterestprofiler.org/), so older descriptions of a 60-item My Next Move website should not be treated as current.

The [2021 O*NET technical manual](https://www.onetcenter.org/dl_files/IP_Manual.pdf), chapters 3–6, documents instrument development, reliability and validity. It describes roughly age 14 as a lower recommended boundary, an eighth-grade reading target, five ordered response categories, and relative six-theme profiles. Its web Short Form sums 10 answers per theme; the Mini-IP sums five. It encourages interpretation alongside other information and exploration over time. Fieldguide’s unknown-answer omission, minimum six rated items per theme, mean 3.5 support threshold, flat-profile tolerance, and editorial field weights are custom decisions, not rules validated by that manual. No performance tasks in the current journey establish measured aptitude.

## Prioritized findings from the application

1. **P1 — Do not label automated branch agreement as external validation.** `professionSuggestions` counts distinct endorsed follow-up questions; at least three supporting questions makes a role eligible, with a specificity tie-break. Broad interest similarity is attached but does not determine this ranking. A student can therefore contradict their earlier interest pattern and still receive a supported role. Test this explicitly, show the conflict as something to explore, and distinguish task-choice support from whole-profile similarity. An override remains legitimate; an unexplained “best match” does not.
2. **P1 — Absolute support thresholds are different from relative-profile linkage.** `interestPicture`/`fieldConnection` depend on absolute endorsement and editorial blends. A differentiated low-rating response style can produce no supported fields, even when its relative pattern is clear. A uniform upward/downward shift should be a diagnostic comparison, not necessarily a hard invariant of the present model. Avoid interpreting “not supported yet” as no suitable careers.
3. **P1 — Values/context are not integrated ranking inputs.** The values choice, team/rhythm/setting and education route questions are collected, but neither broad nor branch ranking uses them. Skills/confidence are explanatory strength clues only. This is acceptable for a preference-led guide if described accurately; it cannot be sold as a combined interest/skills/values aptitude match. Do not add opaque weights merely to make every answer affect rank.
4. **P1 — Unknown, flat and conflicting profiles need non-verdict results.** All-identical, almost-flat, all-untried, selective omissions, contradictory branch choices and universal endorsement must retain clear ways forward without pretending the three displayed cards are three established matches. The current diverse fallback cards are navigation suggestions; preserve that distinction throughout the plan.
5. **P2 — Field blends are editorial and can hide occupational differences.** Health’s Social-heavy blend is not a model of every health occupation. In the embedded O*NET data, family physicians are led by Social/Investigative, while dentists are led by Investigative/Realistic/Social. A hands-on investigative student should still reach dentistry even with modest general helping interest. Similar cautions apply to creative/technical work and organizational occupations.
6. **P2 — Do not treat arbitrary tie order as meaningful precision.** Family array order and occupation array order resolve equal scores. Test tied profiles and label broad alternatives accordingly. The UI should not imply the first card is a scientifically superior answer.

## A genuinely independent occupational benchmark available now

The [October 2025 O*NET Career Returns report](https://www.onetcenter.org/dl_files/IP_Career_Returns.pdf), pp. 4–10, supersedes earlier linkage descriptions. It compares the shape of all six interest scores using profile correlation. Current Mini-IP fit categories use correlations .729, .608 and .426; the lowest category is omitted below .426. Job Zone choices filter preparation level. Flat/identical profiles receive no career matches, with other exploration still available. These are reference-tool rules, not validated thresholds for Fieldguide’s original questions. Correlation is not a probability of success.

The local `occupationEssentials` dataset has all six occupational interest values for 116 of 117 reviewed careers. Tattoo artist (27-1019.00) lacks these values and must appear as unbenchmarked, not have an invented correlation. For each complete non-flat synthetic profile, compute Pearson correlation between six theme means and the six occupational values in fixed RIASEC order. Linear score rescaling does not change correlation. Store source version/date, role, Job Zone, rank, correlation and descriptor coverage. Compare top-10/top-20 role overlap and represented-family overlap; inspect negative-correlation branch suggestions. Report the restricted 117-role universe, not alleged agreement across every O*NET occupation. For ties use sets, not arbitrary ranked equality. Near-flat/partial profiles should be flagged separately rather than awarded definitive comparison labels. A synthetic correlation benchmark checks linkage plausibility; it does not test whether our original questions measure the same constructs in actual students.

## Other established tools: complementary, not interchangeable

| Comparator | Established construct/process | Fair comparison with Fieldguide |
|---|---|---|
| [CareerOneStop Interest Assessment](https://www.careeronestop.org/Toolkit/Careers/interest-assessment.aspx) | Official tools listing describes 30 interest questions. | Compare theme coverage and occupation exploration; do not equate original questions or exact top-three ranks. |
| [CareerOneStop Skills Matcher developer repository](https://github.com/CareerOneStop/Skills-Matcher) and [U.S. DOL February 2026 participant guide](https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/VETS/files/MyNextCareerMove_PG_Interactive_Feb2026.pdf), appendix | Forty self-rated skill/knowledge/ability questions with level examples, producing skill and career lists. | Our 12 practice/confidence cards are not its 40 anchored skill ratings. Low adolescent experience must not be construed as inability to enter a profession after training. |
| [CareerOneStop Work Values Matcher help](https://cloudfront.careeronestop.org/Toolkit/Careers/work-values-matcher-help.aspx) and [work-values definitions](https://cloudfront.careeronestop.org/ExploreCareers/Assessments/work-values.aspx) | Twenty ranked statements compared with occupational work values; six domains: Achievement, Independence, Recognition, Relationships, Support, Working Conditions. | Our “choose up to three” eight priorities are a reflection, not the same rank task or complete domain coverage. Occupational value-fit benchmarking is unavailable from those answers. |

Some CareerOneStop live pages returned access errors to the text browser. Official indexed content, the agency’s own repository and U.S. DOL guide were accessible. No live third-party result agreement was measured. Do not claim that it was.

## Professional standards and the remaining empirical work

[ASCA Ethical Standards, A.14](https://www.schoolcounselor.org/About-School-Counseling/Ethical-Responsibilities/ASCA-Ethical-Standards-for-School-Counselors-(1)) call for valid, reliable, culturally sensitive assessment selection, contextual interpretation and multiple data points rather than treating one result as a student’s future. [NCDA’s 2024 Code of Ethics, E.9](https://www.ncda.org/aws/NCDA/asset_manager/get_file/3395?ver=738703) cautions about insufficient technical evidence, asks practitioners to communicate limits and accurately describe interpretations. These are professional-practice references, not certifications for this app.

After software calibration, invite an appropriately consented high-school pilot with counterbalanced administration of Fieldguide and the official unmodified O*NET instrument. Assess comprehensibility, unknown rates, completion burden, six-scale convergence, test–retest stability and subgroup/exposure differences; have qualified counselors review unexpected recommendations blind to which tool produced them. Predefine analysis and reserve held-out students before tuning weights. No number of synthetic assertions estimates these human properties.

“Exhaustive” must be scoped: 60 interest questions with six answer states alone produce 6^60 patterns before any follow-ups. Exhaustively enumerate reduced scoring states and each finite branch when feasible; use combinatorial coverage, boundary cases and reproducibly sampled complete profiles for the rest, reporting exact coverage and exclusions.

## Licensing boundary

Original questions informed by theory do not inherit official O*NET assessment validation. If replacing them with actual official items later, the [O*NET Tools license](https://www.onetcenter.org/license_tools.html) distinguishes verbatim distribution from modified tools and requires validation for tools incorporating modified content under its developer license. Occupational database descriptors have a separate database license. No instrument-copying change is proposed in this review.
